items.body_md:
On August 24, the SEC issued Release No. 106177 in an administrative proceeding (File No. 3-22435), extending the deadline to submit a Proposed Plan of Distribution — most likely to August 26, 2027 — after the Division received four public comments on a proposed plan it published for comment on June 29, 2026. 
The Commission published a Notice of Proposed Plan of Distribution on June 29, 2026 under Rule 1103, inviting public comment through July 29, 2026, and received four comments raising various issues before issuing this extension on August 24, 2026.
 The practical consequence for Class 5 claimants is significant: the August 20 deadline the SEC faced — under the Second Extension Order (Release No. 104875, February 20, 2026, File No. 3-22382) — has now been superseded, and the Commission's own published distribution methodology will not be finalized for another year. The relationship between File No. 3-22382 (the prior Tai Mo Shan extension orders) and File No. 3-22435 (Release No. 106177) requires confirmation against the full order text; the operative point for recovery posture is that the __[SEC's enforcement docket](https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/admin/2026/34-106177.pdf)__ reflects a further extension well past August 20, meaning no distribution framework for the $123.1 million Fair Fund will issue in the near term.


The plan, once submitted, must define investor eligibility, loss calculations, claim requirements, and payment procedures; the deadline does not trigger payouts. Coordination with Terraform's separate bankruptcy recovery remains unresolved, and claims in the bankruptcy proceeding do not automatically establish eligibility for this fund.
 For Class 5 holders with overlapping losses in both tracks, this extension compounds timing uncertainty: the bankruptcy wind-down runs through December 31, 2026, but the parallel Fair Fund track — which could affect net recovery on duplicate losses — now trails it by a year or more. The SEC's apparent reason for the further extension is the public comment process: 
the Commission published a Notice of Proposed Plan under Rule 1103, with the comment period closing July 29, 2026, suggesting the four comments received required the Division to rework or respond to the proposed methodology before a final plan can be submitted.


Dkt. 1325, filed today, is a rescheduled hearing notice — procedural and routine, carrying no independent effect on recovery or claim allowance. The authorization motion filed August 19 (Dkt. 1321) remains unresolved on the public record, with no corresponding order yet appearing on the docket. The next fixed milestone is December 31, 2026 — the court-extended wind-down deadline — with the Jump Trading litigation and *Chang v. Terraform Labs Wind Down Trust* adversary proceeding the primary substantive resolution triggers ahead of that date. On the Fair Fund track, the operative question is now whether the SEC's next extension order (Release No. 106177) covers the same File No. 3-22382 proceeding as the prior Tai Mo Shan orders, or a distinct but related administrative matter; confirmation would come from the full order text available at the __[SEC enforcement docket](https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/admin/2026/34-106177.pdf)__.

items.body_md:
On August 21, Serrur Investment Partners, LP filed a transfer of claim (Dkt. 1323) in Case No. 24-10070-BLS, Bankr. D. Del., assigning a Class 5 Crypto Loss Claim with a face amount of $3,454,036.42 — the same transferee that filed three prior claim transfers on August 3 (Dkts. 1309–1311) and a Rule 3001(e)(2) notice of transfer for the same claim pool (Dkt. 1312). Dkt. 1323 is a substantive docket event in that it records a change in claim ownership, but it is routine at this stage: it does not alter the aggregate size of the Class 5 pool, the allowance status of the transferred claim, or any recovery percentage. It does confirm that secondary-market buying in Terraform's Crypto Loss Claim pool remains active heading into the fall, with Serrur accumulating at least five discrete transfers since early August. The identity of the transferor is withheld per the notice procedure used in Dkt. 1312, which stated that Serrur holds a signed Evidence of Transfer and will produce it to the Court, the debtors' claims agent, or relevant professionals on written request. Dkt. 1322 is a certificate of mailing and carries no independent significance.

The more consequential open item from the weekend concerns the SEC's Tai Mo Shan Fair Fund. 
The SEC faced an August 20 deadline to submit a plan for distributing the $123.1 million fund paid by Jump Crypto subsidiary Tai Mo Shan to investors harmed by Terra's 2022 collapse.
 
When the SEC extended the deadline in February, it said its staff needed additional time to develop the distribution methodology and, where appropriate, coordinate with anticipated distributions from the Terraform litigation.
 
Coordination with Terraform's separate bankruptcy recovery remains unresolved, and claims in the bankruptcy proceeding do not automatically establish eligibility for this fund.
 No SEC filing confirming submission of the distribution plan has surfaced as of this briefing; confirmation would take the form of a public SEC order or staff submission appearing on the SEC's EDGAR or enforcement docket. The Fair Fund is a parallel recovery track, not a bankruptcy estate asset, but its methodology — particularly how it defines eligible losses and coordinates with plan distributions — will directly affect the net recovery position of Class 5 claimants holding overlapping losses in both processes.

The authorization motion filed August 19 (Dkt. 1321), covered in the prior briefing, remains unresolved on the public record; no order granting or denying it has appeared on the docket. The next fixed milestone remains December 31, 2026 — the court-extended wind-down deadline — with the Jump Trading litigation and the *Chang v. Terraform Labs Wind Down Trust* adversary proceeding the primary near-term resolution triggers ahead of that date. Any SEC submission on the Tai Mo Shan Fair Fund distribution plan, if it landed on or around August 20, would be the most immediately actionable development for claimants to track this week.

items.body_md:
On August 19, the Wind Down Trust filed an authorization motion (Dkt. 1321) before Judge Brendan Linehan Shannon in Case No. 24-10070-BLS, Bankr. D. Del. The full text of Dkt. 1321 was not produced in the document pull, so its precise object cannot be confirmed from the primary record. In a post-confirmation liquidating trust at this stage — with claim reconciliation still active across more than 16,000 Crypto Loss Claims, a $4 billion lawsuit against Jump Trading in progress, and the wind-down phase extended through December 31, 2026 — authorization motions typically seek court approval to take a specific estate action outside the ordinary course of the confirmed plan: executing a significant contract, monetizing an asset, entering a litigation settlement, or making a partial distribution. The applicable standard under the confirmed plan and § 363 of the Bankruptcy Code requires a showing that the action is in the best interests of the estate; no secondary reporting on Dkt. 1321 has surfaced to confirm which action is being authorized. Any reader with PACER access should pull the filing directly to confirm the object before acting on it.

Dkt. 1320, the withdrawal notice filed August 18 and covered yesterday, is the only other entry in the window; it carries no additional significance beyond what was already analyzed. Dkts. 1309–1313 and 1319, previously covered, remain as background. The broader distribution posture is unchanged: 
as of the post-confirmation report for the quarter ending March 31, 2026, the Wind Down Trust had distributed nothing to plan creditors, even as the plan administrator continued reconciling more than 16,000 crypto loss claims and pressing a $4 billion lawsuit against Jump Trading as the estate's largest affirmative recovery effort.
 The next concrete milestone on the calendar is December 31, 2026 — the court-extended deadline for the wind-down phase — with any resolution of the Jump Trading litigation or the *Chang v. Terraform Labs Wind Down Trust* adversary proceeding the more material triggers for distribution timing ahead of that date.

items.body_md:
On August 18, a withdrawal notice (Dkt. 1320) was filed in Case No. 24-10070-BLS before Judge Brendan Linehan Shannon, Bankr. D. Del. The docket line identifies the entry as "Withdrawal - Notice"; the full text of the filing was not pulled, so the specific pleading being withdrawn cannot be confirmed from this record alone. The most likely candidate, given recent docket sequencing, is the objection at Dkt. 1319 (filed August 5), which sits in close proximity and is the only contested filing since the cluster of claim-transfer notices filed August 3 (Dkts. 1309–1313). If Dkt. 1320 withdraws Dkt. 1319, the practical consequence is that whatever challenge was lodged — most plausibly an objection to the Serrur Investment Partners transfer of a $3,454,036.42 Class 5 Crypto Loss Claim (Dkt. 1312) — is now off the table without court resolution, leaving the transfer undisturbed. That outcome is substantive in the narrow sense that a live objection to a claim transfer determines who holds the claim and therefore who receives any distribution, but withdrawal of an unresolved objection is routine on a docket at this scale: it does not change the estate's aggregate liability or the overall distribution pool.

The Serrur transfer itself, docketed July 27 and noticed August 3, transferred a single $3,454,036.42 Class 5 Crypto Loss Claim from an undisclosed transferor to Serrur Investment Partners, LP (37 Greenpoint Avenue, Suite 416, Brooklyn, NY 11222) under Bankruptcy Rule 3001(e)(2). The transferor's identity is withheld from the public record; Serrur represented it holds a signed Evidence of Transfer and will produce it to the court, the debtors, or the claims agent on written request. The claim is one among the more than 16,000 Crypto Loss Claims 
the Wind Down Trust continues reconciling
, and secondary-market transfers of this type signal that at least some claim holders are monetizing positions rather than waiting on distributions — a rational trade given 
distributions have been delayed and the wind-down phase is now officially extended through December 31, 2026.


The broader distribution posture is unchanged. 
As of the post-confirmation report for the quarter ending March 31, 2026, the Wind Down Trust had distributed nothing to plan creditors, even as the plan administrator continued reconciling more than 16,000 crypto loss claims and pressing a $4 billion lawsuit against Jump Trading as the estate's largest affirmative recovery effort.
 The pending adversary proceeding — *Chang v. Terraform Labs PTE. Ltd. Wind Down Trust* — is still before Judge Shannon following the plan administrator's July motion to dismiss, __[Law360, July 20, 2026](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy-authority/mid-cap/articles/2504885)__. The next concrete milestone on the recovery timeline is December 31, 2026, the court-extended deadline for the wind-down phase; any material movement in the Jump Trading litigation or the Chang adversary ahead of that date would be the more significant trigger for distribution timing.

items.body_md:
*In re Terraform Labs Pte. Ltd., Bankr. D. Del., Case No. 24-10070-BLS, Judge Brendan Linehan Shannon*

The only new docket activity since Wednesday's edition is Dkt. 1319, an Objection filed August 5, 2026. The docket entry designation — "Objection" without further qualification in the publicly available record — places it squarely in the pattern that has defined this estate's post-confirmation phase: contested claim allowance, disputed claim transfers, or resistance to a pending motion. The filing lands two days after a cluster of four claim transfers (Dkts. 1309–1312, August 3), the most recent of which assigned a $3,454,036.42 claim from a redacted transferor to Serrur Investment Partners, LP via TerraClaim LLC, signaling continued secondary-market activity in the claims pool. Whether Dkt. 1319 targets one of those transfers, challenges a valuation determination on the crypto loss claims register, or contests some other pending matter cannot be confirmed from publicly available sources as of this briefing; the filing's substance requires PACER access to the full document.

What is clear is the structural context: 
more than two years after Terraform Labs entered chapter 11, its confirmed liquidating plan remains in active administration, and as of the post-confirmation report for the quarter ending March 31, 2026, the Wind Down Trust had distributed nothing to plan creditors, even as the plan administrator continued reconciling more than 16,000 crypto loss claims and pressing a $4 billion lawsuit against Jump Trading as the estate's largest affirmative recovery effort
 (__[Elevenflo](https://elevenflo.com/blog/terraform-labs-bankruptcy)__). An objection at Dkt. 1319 — whatever its precise target — lands in an estate where claim allowance determinations are the direct gating mechanism for eventual distributions. Any successful objection that disallows or reduces a claim expands the recoverable pool for remaining allowed creditors; any objection that fails preserves a competing draw on that pool. The post-confirmation reports filed July 30 (Dkts. 1306–1307) will also repay review once accessible, as they will reflect the trust's asset position for the most recent quarterly period and may reveal whether the cash runway supports the litigation posture in the Jump and Jane Street proceedings.

The next concrete milestone to track is any response deadline or hearing date tied to Dkt. 1319, which under Local Rule 9006-1(c) would typically run 14 days from service absent a separate scheduling order. On the litigation front, the plan administrator's motion to dismiss the Chang adversary proceeding (Adv. Proc. 26-50229) remains pending before Judge Shannon following the July 2026 filing reported last month (__[Law360](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy-authority/mid-cap/articles/2504885)__), and the Jane Street insider-trading action in the Southern District of New York continues to be contested on the motion-to-dismiss briefing that closed in June (__[Law360](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy/articles/2489043)__). Neither of those proceedings generated new docket activity in the lookback window.
